The lived symptom is not abstract tidiness: provisioning instance 1 of anything today means finding and editing nine files, and a shipped app whose root is not under Akien's home directory cannot run at all, because nine of ten sites bake in Path.home(). Akien's stated reason (II) for the four-rung ruling — 'it leaves open the possibility to expand in the future without rearchitecting that part' — is bought in the DIRECTORY LAYOUT and is not bought in the CODE. This ticket buys the code half.
traces_to: Law 1 ('the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled; re-deriving a settled answer is a defect') as the primary trace, and the 2026-08-12 ruling's own reason (II) as the proximate one. Partially Law 4 — but only partially, and the ticket is cast saying so: the resolver is a convenience until something REFUSES the alternative, which is child (b).
falsifier: DONE, two runnable measures, both at PROVEME by the proof and not by narration: (a) resolving instance 1 of any device requires editing zero path-building sites — checked by pointing the injected roots at a temp dir and resolving device+instance without touching a caller; (b) a grep for Path.home() with '.cairn' and for expanduser('~/.cairn') across non-proof code returns only the resolver module itself, plus the dispositioned inference_domain site. WRONG: the resolver becomes an ELEVENTH place a path is built rather than the only one — the sites keep their hand-spelled copies and the two shapes drift. That failure is already observed in miniature (see measured_at_cast.the_drift_is_not_hypothetical), which is what makes it a live falsifier rather than a decorative one.
